recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-3731 unless PA/MnM later changes the birth-time extension in the Extension Pack.
issue_request: FHIR-3731 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for the DSTU1 request to separate Patient birth date from birth time by changing the date of birth field from dateTime to date.
initial_application: Historical commit 782b46a25e1bb69e60c5ca845b707ac444136651 explicitly mentions tracker #3731 and changed the legacy Patient spreadsheet source for Patient.birthDate from dateTime to date. Later refactors moved the authoritative Patient definition to source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml while preserving that type.
additional_context: Patient is active in source/fhir.ini. Current Patient.birthDate is type date, its short/definition say date of birth, and its comment points time-of-birth use cases to patient-birthTime. Related later issues FHIR-5544 and FHIR-7301 retained the date-only core design and used standard extension guidance; FHIR-7301 already has a combined-branch audit. The patient-birthTime StructureDefinition now lives in the FHIR Extension Pack with Patient.birthDate context and a dateTime value.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit on the combined branch. Recreating the moved birth-time extension in core or changing Patient.birthDate would be contrary to the current source and later related decisions.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Patient/Practitioner issue fixed birthDate wording and added the birthTime extension guidance that complements the FHIR-3731 type change.

Later Published request to make Patient.birthDate dateTime was rejected with modification in favor of date plus standard birth-time extension guidance; commit 8b5ebacf18d43df3464a37ef994f7f62c21f656c already audits it on the combined branch.
Duplicate request for dateTime/clarification resolved as a duplicate of FHIR-7301.
No-change neonate birth date/time question confirmed that Patient BirthTime guidance was the intended answer.
